paper.abstract_en: The two-sphere partition function of timelike Liouville theory admits two complementary semi-classical descriptions whose relation presents a non-perturbative puzzle. A direct path-integral expansion around the round two-sphere saddle reproduces the perturbative small-$β$ expansion, with $β$ the Liouville coupling, of the analytically continued Dorn-Otto-Zamolodchikov-Zamolodchikov (DOZZ) formula, while the latter contains an additional oscillatory factor suggestive of a second saddle contribution. We investigate the origin of this factor in the Liouville zero-mode sector using Picard-Lefschetz theory. Taking as input the Hankel-type contour motivated by the inverse-Gamma representation of the zero-mode integral, we determine its Lefschetz-thimble decomposition depending on $β$. For $0<β<1$, it precisely reproduces the saddle structure encoded in the analytically continued DOZZ result. We identify the integration contour as the source of the difference between the zero-mode saddle descriptions. As $β$ approaches $1$, the zero-mode saddle moves to the boundary of field space, while for $β>1$ the same contour is represented by a single contributing thimble. We further relate this Stokes reorganisation to recent probabilistic constructions of timelike Liouville theory.
